1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide __that is heterologous to the cell__.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo __from heterologous polynucleotides__.

3. (Original) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme.

4. (Original) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 or claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence __and is heterologous to the cell__.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide __that is heterologous to the cell__.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide __and the EutS polypeptide is heterologous to the cell__.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides __from different bacterial species or different BMC operons__.

9. (Original) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species.

10. (Original) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag __and is heterologous to the cell__.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide __for the purpose of engineering a new metabolic capability in the host cell__.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium.

14. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae.

15. (Original) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli.

16. (Original) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast __and the BMC polypeptides are heterologous to the yeast__.

18. (Original) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae.

19. (Original) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga __and the BMC polypeptides are heterologous to the alga__.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one heterologous bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one heterologous enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one heterologous enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product __for the purpose of producing the product in a compartmentalized manner__.

22. (Original) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product.

23. (Original) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor.

24. (Original) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one heterologous enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate __and the non-native compartment sequesters a toxic intermediate product__.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments __by virtue of the affinity tag on the BMC polypeptides__.

27. (Original) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments __wherein each compartment comprises heterologous BMC polypeptides__.
